task: edit a video in a video editor (CapCut, iMovie, DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Clipchamp): import footage, make concrete edits — trim or split clips, add captions or text, add music or adjust audio, apply transitions or speed changes — and export the result; complete when the export finishes (the saved/share screen or the rendered file is shown). Surface pinned: the editing session itself — not editing-theory talks, not before/after showcases without the session. One-click AI editing flows (auto-edit, AI video generators like Sora or Runway) are off-task; ordinary tool features such as auto-captions used inside a manual edit are fine.

tree.label: Edit and export video
tree.note: 1 prepares the project and 2 gathers the media; use 3 to assemble the sequence; repeat 3 through 6 in the order the edit needs, checking the result with 7 after each meaningful change and saving progress with 9.1; do 8 when the reviewed edit is ready; return from 8 to the relevant editing goal if the export exposes a problem; use 9.2 through 9.5 only when separately asked to manage saved projects or source files

children.label: Prepare the project
children.note: 1.1 opens the editor and 1.2 resolves account access where required; use 1.3 and 1.4 for a new project or 1.5 to resume one; check 1.6 and 1.7 before detailed editing; 1.8 can repeat whenever the required controls are hidden

questions.question: Is the editor using the account intended for this project?
questions.why: Project media could be stored in another account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Project media could be stored in another account.
questions.check: What is the signed-in account identity? A sign-in provider button does not prove the account used.
questions.say_example: The editor is signed in as <account>. This project was meant for <requested account>.

questions.question: Do you want to connect this account to the editor?
questions.why: The editor could receive unapproved access to an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The editor could receive unapproved access to an account.
questions.verify_form: Does connecting this account to the editor have your authorization?
questions.check: What do the account-connection prompt, receiving app, account identity, and requested permissions show?
questions.say_example: <Editor> is asking for <access> to <account>. Allow that connection?

questions.question: Did the agent create the kind of project you requested?
questions.why: The editor may generate or constrain the sequence in ways you did not request.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The editor may generate or constrain the sequence in ways you did not request.
questions.check: What are the selected project mode or template name and the available editing controls?
questions.say_example: This project uses <mode>. Your request needs <requested mode>.

questions.question: Does the saved project have the name you requested?
questions.why: The project may be difficult to find when editing resumes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The project may be difficult to find when editing resumes.
questions.check: What is the saved project name in the title or project listing?
questions.say_example: Named the project <Weekend Recap> - you asked for <Beach Day Edit>

questions.question: Is the agent working in the project you meant to edit?
questions.why: Changes could be made to a different project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Changes could be made to a different project.
questions.check: What are the active project name and any displayed location or distinguishing date?
questions.say_example: The open project is <actual>. You asked me to edit <requested>.

questions.question: Does the canvas shape match the requested video?
questions.why: The finished video could have the wrong shape.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The finished video could have the wrong shape.
questions.check: What are the selected canvas width and height or aspect ratio?
questions.say_example: The canvas is <actual ratio>. You asked for <requested ratio>.

questions.question: Does the timeline format match the agreed editing settings?
questions.why: The sequence may be edited at the wrong size or frame rate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The sequence may be edited at the wrong size or frame rate.
questions.check: What are the active timeline resolution and frame rate, separately from source and export settings?
questions.say_example: The timeline uses <actual setting>. We agreed on <requested setting>.

questions.question: Do you want to make this change now, before it's hard to undo?
questions.why: Later edits may have to be recreated to change this setting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Later edits may have to be recreated to change this setting.
questions.verify_form: Does this format change require a decision before it becomes difficult to undo?
questions.check: What are the proposed setting and the exact warning about undoing or changing it later?
questions.say_example: The editor says <warning>. Change the timeline to <setting>?

children.label: Gather source media
children.note: 2.1 identifies a source; if that source is a stock or library asset, use 2.4 and 2.5 first to find it and check its cost; then use 2.2 to inspect candidates and 2.3 to import the selected files; 2.6 and 2.7 check what arrived; use 2.8 when media is missing; repeat this goal whenever another asset is needed

questions.question: Do the selected files contain the footage you asked to use?
questions.why: The finished edit could use the wrong people, event, or take.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The finished edit could use the wrong people, event, or take.
questions.check: What people, setting, action, or subject do the clip's or generated image's preview thumbnail or filename/label show?
questions.say_example: This clip shows <observed content>. You asked for <requested content>.

questions.question: Did the media arrive in the intended project or library?
questions.why: The intended project may still be missing its source media.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The intended project may still be missing its source media.
questions.check: What are the destination project or library name and the imported file listing?
questions.say_example: Imported files into <Untitled Project 2> - the edit is in <Weekend Recap>

questions.question: Do the selected filenames match the sources you requested?
questions.why: The wrong source could be imported before its contents are reviewed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The wrong source could be imported before its contents are reviewed.
questions.check: What are the selected filenames and displayed source locations?
questions.say_example: The selection includes <actual file>. You requested <requested file>.

questions.question: Does a selected asset or feature add a cost you have not approved?
questions.why: Finishing the edit may require payment or replacement of the selected item.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Finishing the edit may require payment or replacement of the selected item.
questions.check: What are the selected asset or feature name and its displayed price or subscription requirement?
questions.say_example: <Selected item> requires <paid plan or price>. That cost has not been approved.

questions.question: Do you want to approve this purchase?
questions.why: The user could be charged once or repeatedly for something they did not agree to pay for.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user could be charged once or repeatedly for something they did not agree to pay for.
questions.verify_form: Does this paid plan or asset purchase have your authorization?
questions.check: What are the selected paid item or plan, total charge, billing period, and renewal terms when applicable?
questions.say_example: <Item or plan> costs <price>, with <billing terms>. Make this purchase?

questions.question: Is the source long enough for the passage the edit requires?
questions.why: The edit cannot include that passage without another source or a changed request.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The edit cannot include that passage without another source or a changed request.
questions.check: What are the source identity, total duration, and selected in and out points, with units?
questions.say_example: This source ends at <source end>. The requested passage continues to <requested end>.

questions.question: Is any required media missing or offline?
questions.why: The export may contain a missing-media screen or omit part of the edit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The export may contain a missing-media screen or omit part of the edit.
questions.check: What are the exact missing-media warning and any named files?
questions.say_example: The editor cannot find <file>. That part of the video is not ready to export.

children.label: Assemble the timeline
children.note: 3.1 and 3.2 establish the sequence; repeat 3.3 for passages that need trimming; 3.4 adds or protects layers; use 3.5 for an intentional copy and 3.6 to revert an unwanted change; 3.7 supplies a background where needed; check the changed sequence with 7 before continuing

questions.question: Did inserting or pasting this clip replace footage that should stay?
questions.why: Part of the earlier edit could disappear without being noticed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Part of the earlier edit could disappear without being noticed.
questions.check: What are the edit mode used for the drop (Insert or Overwrite) and the sequence duration immediately before and after the action?
questions.say_example: Adding <clip> replaced <earlier passage>. That passage was meant to stay.

questions.question: Did the insertion include the required video and audio?
questions.why: A clip may have no sound, no picture, or an extra sound track.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A clip may have no sound, no picture, or an extra sound track.
questions.check: Does the timeline entry for the added clip have a video segment, an audio segment, or both?
questions.say_example: <Clip> was added without <required component>.

questions.question: Does the sequence keep the order you requested?
questions.why: The video may tell the story in the wrong order.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video may tell the story in the wrong order.
questions.check: What are the clip names or labels on the timeline in left-to-right order?
questions.say_example: <Clip> now appears <actual position>. It was meant to appear <requested position>.

children.label: Trim the selected clips
children.note: 3.3.1 identifies what to keep; 3.3.2 selects a source range before insertion where useful; 3.3.3 divides the timeline clip or 3.3.4 changes its edges; 3.3.5 removes unwanted footage; use 3.3.6 only when the remaining gap should close; repeat and review the cut with 7.2

questions.question: Does the selected passage include the moments you asked to keep?
questions.why: An important part of the requested footage could be omitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An important part of the requested footage could be omitted.
questions.check: What does the source preview at the selected in and out points show, compared with the specific moment named in the request?
questions.say_example: The selected passage leaves out <required moment>.

questions.question: Do the selected source boundaries match the requested timestamps?
questions.why: The inserted passage could begin or end at the wrong moment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The inserted passage could begin or end at the wrong moment.
questions.check: What are the selected source identity and source in and out times, separately from sequence time?
questions.say_example: The source selection runs from <actual in> to <actual out>. You requested <requested range>.

questions.question: Did the split affect the intended tracks at the same sequence time?
questions.why: Later trimming could move the camera angles or audio apart.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Later trimming could move the camera angles or audio apart.
questions.check: What is the sequence time at which each track (video and any linked audio) was split?
questions.say_example: <Track> was split at <actual time>. The other intended tracks were split at <target time>.

questions.question: Did trimming remove a word or action that should be kept?
questions.why: The sentence or action may become incomplete or change meaning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The sentence or action may become incomplete or change meaning.
questions.check: What do the frames or waveform immediately before and after the trimmed edge show for the word or action named in the request?
questions.say_example: The cut removes <word or action> at <time>. It belongs to the passage you wanted to keep.

questions.question: Did the editor add a promotion at the end that you did not ask to keep?
questions.why: The delivered video could contain an unwanted advertisement.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video could contain an unwanted advertisement.
questions.check: Does the timeline immediately after the requested ending show an automatically added clip, bumper, or watermark?
questions.say_example: An editor promotion follows your ending at <time>.

questions.question: Did deleting the passage preserve the intended gap or join?
questions.why: The edit may introduce an empty frame or remove an intended pause.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The edit may introduce an empty frame or remove an intended pause.
questions.check: Does the timeline show a gap or joined edit at the point of the deletion, and what is its duration if a gap remains?
questions.say_example: The deletion <left or removed> the gap from <start> to <end>. You asked to <close or preserve> it.

questions.question: Did deletion change a retained clip or title outside the intended removal?
questions.why: A title, cutaway, or audio cue may disappear or play at the wrong time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A title, cutaway, or audio cue may disappear or play at the wrong time.
questions.check: What are the duration and start time of the retained clip, title, or audio cue immediately outside the deleted passage, before and after the deletion?
questions.say_example: Deleting that passage also changed <retained layer> from <before> to <after>.

children.label: Arrange the media layers
children.note: 3.4.1 creates tracks where necessary; 3.4.2 places the overlay on the intended layer; 3.4.3 selects how it appears; 3.4.4 controls which tracks can be changed or heard; check the result with 7.3 and 7.4

questions.question: Does the overlay show the intended content without hiding something that must remain visible?
questions.why: The viewer could miss the main action or explanation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer could miss the main action or explanation.
questions.check: What does the overlay cover in the composed frame at the relevant time?
questions.say_example: <Overlay> covers <required content> at <time>.

questions.question: Are the tracks needed for this operation protected or enabled as intended?
questions.why: An unrelated part of the sequence could change.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An unrelated part of the sequence could change.
questions.check: Which tracks are included, locked, or muted for this operation?
questions.say_example: This operation includes <track>, which was meant to stay unchanged.

questions.question: Did undo restore the intended change without undoing later work you wanted to keep?
questions.why: The correction may leave the original mistake or remove additional work.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The correction may leave the original mistake or remove additional work.
questions.check: What do the timeline or edit history immediately before and after the undo action show, for the specific change it reports reverting?
questions.say_example: Undo also removed <retained change>. That change was meant to stay.

questions.question: Does the background cover the intended title or sequence interval?
questions.why: Part of a title or ending may appear against the wrong background.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Part of a title or ending may appear against the wrong background.
questions.check: What are the start and end time of the background clip, against the start and end time of the title or sequence interval it should cover?
questions.say_example: The background ends at <time>, while <title or layer> continues to <end>.

children.label: Adjust the picture
children.note: use 4.1 for composition, 4.2 for playback timing, 4.3 for color, 4.4 for visual effects, and 4.5 for transitions; these branches are optional and can repeat in any order; a timing change requires another pass through 6 and 7

children.label: Frame the visible content
children.note: 4.1.1 chooses what remains in frame; 4.1.2 sets its placement and scale; 4.1.3 changes orientation where needed; 4.1.4 adds motion only when wanted; review the visible content with 7.3

questions.question: Does the crop preserve the content that must remain visible?
questions.why: The viewer could lose part of the action, slide, or explanation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer could lose part of the action, slide, or explanation.
questions.check: What falls inside versus outside the crop boundary in the cropped frame at the relevant time?
questions.say_example: The crop cuts off <required content> at <time>.

questions.question: Does the position and scale preserve the requested framing?
questions.why: The subject or demonstration may be difficult to see.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The subject or demonstration may be difficult to see.
questions.check: What falls outside the visible frame in the framed result at the relevant time?
questions.say_example: <Required content> is outside the frame at <time>.

questions.question: Is the resulting image oriented as requested?
questions.why: The shot or text may become difficult to understand.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The shot or text may become difficult to understand.
questions.check: Does the flipped frame show any on-screen text or asymmetric detail, and what is its orientation?
questions.say_example: The flip reversed <visible text> in the picture.

questions.question: Does the animated framing keep following the intended subject?
questions.why: The camera movement could hide the part of the shot you wanted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The camera movement could hide the part of the shot you wanted.
questions.check: Does the framed result across the animated range keep the intended subject inside the frame?
questions.say_example: The framing loses <subject> from <start> to <end>.

children.label: Change the playback timing
children.note: 4.2.1 changes constant speed or 4.2.2 varies speed across the clip; use 4.2.3 to reverse and 4.2.4 to hold a frame; check resulting duration with 7.5 and sound with 7.4

questions.question: Was the requested playback speed applied to the intended clip?
questions.why: The wrong passage could play too quickly or too slowly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The wrong passage could play too quickly or too slowly.
questions.check: What are the selected clip identity and speed value, including whether the value is a percentage or multiplier?
questions.say_example: <Clip> is set to <actual speed>. You asked for <requested speed>.

questions.question: Did the speed change preserve the intended timing of the rest of the sequence?
questions.why: Other clips or audio cues may no longer line up.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Other clips or audio cues may no longer line up.
questions.check: What is the sequence time of a later clip or audio cue before and after the speed change?
questions.say_example: Changing the speed moved <later cue> from <before> to <after>.

questions.question: Did the speed change preserve the intended voice and sound?
questions.why: The voice may sound different or become hard to understand.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The voice may sound different or become hard to understand.
questions.check: When listening to the sped-up passage, do the words remain distinguishable, and is pitch correction enabled?
questions.say_example: The speed change makes <passage> hard to understand.

questions.question: Does the speed ramp preserve the important action and its intended timing?
questions.why: The effect could obscure the action it was meant to emphasize.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The effect could obscure the action it was meant to emphasize.
questions.check: Do the frames at each speed-ramp node show the action named in the request as visible or obscured?
questions.say_example: The speed ramp passes over <required action> at <time>.

questions.question: Does reversing this passage produce the requested result?
questions.why: Speech or action could run backward unintentionally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Speech or action could run backward unintentionally.
questions.check: When viewing or listening to the reversed passage, what plays backward?
questions.say_example: <Passage> now plays backward, including <component that should remain forward>.

questions.question: Does the freeze frame hold the intended image for the requested time?
questions.why: The pause could emphasize the wrong moment or interrupt the sequence.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The pause could emphasize the wrong moment or interrupt the sequence.
questions.check: What are the frozen frame's timestamp and the hold duration?
questions.say_example: Held the frame at <0:42> for <2 seconds> - you asked for <3 seconds>

children.label: Adjust the clip color
children.note: 4.3.1 handles source color profiles where offered; 4.3.2 balances color and 4.3.3 makes manual adjustments; 4.3.4 applies a preset if wanted; use 4.3.5 to compare or reset before keeping the change

questions.question: Does the selected color conversion match the source recording format?
questions.why: The conversion could produce the wrong color or brightness.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The conversion could produce the wrong color or brightness.
questions.check: What are the source clip's recorded color format or profile and the color-space conversion applied to it?
questions.say_example: The source is recorded as <source format>. The selected conversion expects <different format>.

questions.question: Was the requested color preset applied at the agreed strength?
questions.why: The clip could use a different look than the one chosen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The clip could use a different look than the one chosen.
questions.check: What are the selected clip, applied preset name, and strength value?
questions.say_example: Applied <Cinematic> at <70%> to <clip 3> - you asked for <100%>

questions.question: Did the color adjustment preserve the detail and appearance the edit needs?
questions.why: Important image detail or a requested appearance could be lost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Important image detail or a requested appearance could be lost.
questions.check: Does the adjusted frame at the relevant passage still show detail that was visible before the adjustment?
questions.say_example: The adjustment hides <required detail> in <affected passage>.

questions.question: Is the preview showing your color adjustments right now?
questions.why: The displayed preview could hide the changes being checked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The displayed preview could hide the changes being checked.
questions.check: Is color-grade bypass enabled or disabled? The button label alone does not show whether bypass is active.
questions.say_example: Color adjustments are bypassed. This preview is showing the ungraded result.

children.label: Apply the visual effects
children.note: 4.4.1 manages the effect stack for whichever effects the edit needs; 4.4.2 changes blending, 4.4.3 changes values over time, 4.4.4 stabilizes motion, 4.4.5 changes appearance, and 4.4.6 isolates a subject, each used only when needed; review each result with 7.3

questions.question: Does the visual effect preserve the content it was meant to enhance?
questions.why: The effect could make the scene harder to understand.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The effect could make the scene harder to understand.
questions.check: What does the frame with the effect applied at the relevant time cover or obscure?
questions.say_example: <Effect> hides <required content> from <start> to <end>.

questions.question: Did the required effect fail to load or apply?
questions.why: The requested appearance may be absent from the edit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The requested appearance may be absent from the edit.
questions.check: What are the exact load or application error and the affected effect name?
questions.say_example: The editor reports <error> for <effect>. That effect has not been confirmed.

questions.question: Does the selected effect setting match the value you requested?
questions.why: The agent’s chosen effect could differ from your explicit instruction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent’s chosen effect could differ from your explicit instruction.
questions.check: What are the selected clip, applied effect name, and the particular parameter named in the request?
questions.say_example: <Effect parameter> is set to <actual value>. You requested <requested value>.

questions.question: Does the blend or opacity change leave the intended layers visible?
questions.why: The viewer could lose information carried by a layer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer could lose information carried by a layer.
questions.check: Which layer, if any, is no longer visible in the composited frame at the relevant time?
questions.say_example: <Layer> disappears at <time> after the opacity change.

questions.question: Does the selected opacity match the requested value?
questions.why: A layer could be more or less visible than intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A layer could be more or less visible than intended.
questions.check: What are the selected layer and opacity at the requested time?
questions.say_example: Set <the overlay> to <60%> opacity at <1:12> - you asked for <40%>

questions.question: Did stabilization reduce the unwanted movement without losing important content?
questions.why: A steadier shot could still lose or distort the subject.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A steadier shot could still lose or distort the subject.
questions.check: Does the stabilized frame across the shot keep the subject framed and undistorted?
questions.say_example: The stabilized shot still has <observed problem> at <time>.

questions.question: Did retouching change only the subject and features you intended?
questions.why: Someone’s appearance or the scene could be altered beyond the request.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Someone’s appearance or the scene could be altered beyond the request.
questions.check: Which features or subjects changed in the retouched frame compared with the original?
questions.say_example: The retouch also changes <unrequested feature or subject>.

questions.question: Does the mask preserve the intended subject throughout the shot?
questions.why: The cutout could remove part of the person or leave unwanted content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The cutout could remove part of the person or leave unwanted content.
questions.check: Does the masked frame across the shot show any part of the subject missing?
questions.say_example: The mask removes <part of the subject> from <start> to <end>.

questions.question: Would stopping now throw away work you haven't agreed to lose?
questions.why: Completed edits may have to be recreated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Completed edits may have to be recreated.
questions.verify_form: Would stopping this process discard work you have not agreed to lose?
questions.check: What work does the cancellation warning say will be discarded?
questions.say_example: Stopping will discard <work named in warning>. Stop anyway?

questions.question: Does the requested redaction cover the information throughout the affected passage?
questions.why: The delivered video could reveal information you asked to remove.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video could reveal information you asked to remove.
questions.check: When viewing or listening to the affected passage across its full duration, is the information named for redaction still visible or audible at any point?
questions.say_example: The redaction at <time> is incomplete. <Type of information> remains visible or audible.

children.label: Connect the adjacent clips
children.note: 4.5.1 chooses a transition or a hard cut; 4.5.2 sets the affected cut and duration; 4.5.3 finishes the final image; review transitions with 7.2 and return to 3.3 if more source footage is needed

questions.question: Does the transition match the chosen effect, cut, and duration?
questions.why: The wrong cut could receive the effect or its timing could change.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The wrong cut could receive the effect or its timing could change.
questions.check: What are the transition's applied effect, the cut it sits on, and its duration?
questions.say_example: Applied a <1 second> transition at <the second cut> - you asked for <0.5 seconds>

questions.question: Does the transition freeze or repeat a frame it shouldn't?
questions.why: The cut may appear to stop or jump.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The cut may appear to stop or jump.
questions.check: Does any frame the transition uses repeat or freeze where source footage should continue?
questions.say_example: The transition shows <unintended frozen or repeated image> at <time>.

children.label: Add text and graphics
children.note: 5.1 selects a title style and 5.2 sets its words; 5.3 controls typography, 5.4 placement, and 5.5 timing; use 5.6 for captions and 5.7 for stickers; check with 5.8 whether the text stays readable as the background changes

questions.question: Does the title use the wording you approved?
questions.why: The video could display the wrong name or message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video could display the wrong name or message.
questions.check: What is the title text in the editor’s text field, without assuming every word is visible in playback?
questions.say_example: The title says <actual wording>. You approved <requested wording>.

questions.question: Does the title use the style you asked for?
questions.why: The title could violate the requested visual style.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The title could violate the requested visual style.
questions.check: What are the selected title’s font, color, or template for the specified property?
questions.say_example: Set the title's <color> to <white> - you asked for <yellow>

questions.question: Does the title appear with the intended passage for long enough to read it?
questions.why: The text may be missed or attached to the wrong scene.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The text may be missed or attached to the wrong scene.
questions.check: What are the title's on-screen start and end time, against the start and end time of the passage it belongs with?
questions.say_example: <Title> appears during <actual passage>. It belongs with <intended passage>.

questions.question: Will generating captions overwrite corrections you already made?
questions.why: Names and wording already corrected could be lost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Names and wording already corrected could be lost.
questions.verify_form: Will generating captions replace corrections that should be retained?
questions.check: What are the selected caption source, existing caption status, and explicit replacement setting or warning?
questions.say_example: Generating captions will replace <existing captions>. Replace them?

questions.question: Do the captions match the spoken words?
questions.why: People relying on captions may receive the wrong information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: People relying on captions may receive the wrong information.
questions.check: What is the caption text at a given time, against the words spoken in the audio at that time?
questions.say_example: At <time>, the caption says <caption>. The audio says <spoken words>.

questions.question: Do captions appear with the words they represent?
questions.why: People relying on captions could attribute words to the wrong scene or speaker.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: People relying on captions could attribute words to the wrong scene or speaker.
questions.check: What is the caption's displayed time range, against the time range in which its words are actually spoken?
questions.say_example: The caption <caption> appears at <caption time>. Its words are spoken at <speech time>.

questions.question: Do the captions use the audio and language you asked for?
questions.why: The generated captions could describe another track or use the wrong language.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The generated captions could describe another track or use the wrong language.
questions.check: What are the selected caption audio source and language settings?
questions.say_example: Captions are set to use <actual source or language>. You requested <requested value>.

questions.question: Can the captions be read in the video at the intended viewing size?
questions.why: People relying on captions could miss part of the spoken content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: People relying on captions could miss part of the spoken content.
questions.check: Is any character in the caption at the relevant time, against its background, obscured or cut off?
questions.say_example: The caption at <time> has <observed reading problem>.

questions.question: Does the added graphic show the intended mark without covering required content?
questions.why: The video could show the wrong identity or hide part of the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video could show the wrong identity or hide part of the message.
questions.check: What does the placed graphic cover in the frame?
questions.say_example: <Graphic> covers <required content> at <time>.

questions.question: Can the title be read throughout the time it appears?
questions.why: The viewer may miss the title’s message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer may miss the title’s message.
questions.check: Viewed against the video behind it throughout its on-screen duration, is there any point where the title becomes hard to distinguish from the background?
questions.say_example: <Words> become hard to read against <background> at <time>.

questions.question: Will destination controls cover important text or graphics?
questions.why: The title or captions could be hidden when the video is watched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The title or captions could be hidden when the video is watched.
questions.check: When the preview shows the destination platform's interface elements (such as a caption bar or button overlay), do they cover the title or graphics?
questions.say_example: <Destination control> covers <text or graphic> in this preview.

children.label: Mix the soundtrack
children.note: 6.1 gathers audio or 6.2 records narration; use 6.3 to balance and process it, and 6.4 to align it with the picture; repeat 6.3 and 6.4 after changes to clip length or order; use 7.4 to review the complete mix

children.label: Gather the audio sources
children.note: 6.1.1 finds and previews music; 6.1.2 checks the available rights and cost information; 6.1.3 imports the chosen file; 6.1.4 selects sound effects; return to these operations if the sound does not suit the edit

questions.question: Is this connection asking for more access than you agreed to?
questions.why: Another app could receive access to the account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Another app could receive access to the account.
questions.verify_form: Does connecting the sound library grant only the access you approved?
questions.check: What are the account identity, receiving app, and permission scope in the actual authorization prompt?
questions.say_example: <App> is asking for <access> to <account>. Allow that connection?

questions.question: Do the displayed music terms cover the intended use?
questions.why: The music may need replacing before the video can be delivered as requested.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The music may need replacing before the video can be delivered as requested.
questions.check: What are the asset’s stated allowed uses and restrictions? A search filter or automated copyright pass does not establish permission.
questions.say_example: The terms for <track> exclude <requested use>. We need a track whose terms cover it.

questions.question: Is the soundtrack the track and passage you asked to use?
questions.why: The video could use different music or the wrong version of a track.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video could use different music or the wrong version of a track.
questions.check: What are the track name and selected passage shown in the music browser or timeline?
questions.say_example: The edit uses <actual track or passage>. You selected <requested track or passage>.

questions.question: Is the selected audio file the one you specified?
questions.why: The edit could use another recording or music version.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The edit could use another recording or music version.
questions.check: What are the selected audio filename and displayed location or version?
questions.say_example: The selected audio is <actual file>. You requested <requested file>.

questions.question: Does the sound effect match the intended event and passage?
questions.why: The added sound could misrepresent or obscure the scene.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The added sound could misrepresent or obscure the scene.
questions.check: What does the selected sound-effect variation sound like, against the moment it is meant to accompany?
questions.say_example: The sound at <time> suggests <observed event>. You asked for <intended sound>.

children.label: Record the narration
children.note: 6.2.1 chooses the input and target track; 6.2.2 checks that sound reaches the recorder; then use 6.2.3 for the take and review it with 7.4

questions.question: Is the voiceover recording using the intended input and destination track?
questions.why: The take may capture the wrong source or record onto the wrong track.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The take may capture the wrong source or record onto the wrong track.
questions.check: What are the selected input device, armed track, and recording destination?
questions.say_example: Recording is set to <actual device and track>. The intended setup is <requested setup>.

questions.question: Does a short test recording capture the voice clearly?
questions.why: A complete voiceover take could be unusable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A complete voiceover take could be unusable.
questions.check: When listening to a short test recording, is there any audible problem such as noise, clipping, or silence?
questions.say_example: The test recording contains <observed problem>. The main take is not ready to start.

questions.question: Does the retained voiceover contain the complete take you asked to use?
questions.why: The narration could omit or repeat part of the explanation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The narration could omit or repeat part of the explanation.
questions.check: What does the retained voiceover take sound like, against the script or passage it was meant to cover?
questions.say_example: The retained voiceover <omits or repeats> <phrase> at <time>.

children.label: Balance the audio tracks
children.note: 6.3.1 separates audio when independent editing is needed; 6.3.2 sets levels; 6.3.3 controls temporary muting; 6.3.4 adjusts processing; restore the intended track states before the complete playback check

questions.question: Did editing linked or detached media preserve the intended picture and sound timing?
questions.why: The voice or scene sound could play at the wrong time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The voice or scene sound could play at the wrong time.
questions.check: What are the timeline positions of the audio component and its paired video component after the edit?
questions.say_example: <Audio or video component> moved by <offset> while its paired component stayed in place.

questions.question: Is the required speech understandable at the intended listening level?
questions.why: The viewer may be unable to follow the spoken content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer may be unable to follow the spoken content.
questions.check: When listening to the dialogue at the current levels, is any word inaudible or distorted?
questions.say_example: The words at <time range> are <observed listening problem>.

questions.question: Does the audio level setting match the value and scope you requested?
questions.why: The change could affect the wrong sound or more clips than intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The change could affect the wrong sound or more clips than intended.
questions.check: What are the selected clip or track and its level value with units, and does the change apply to one clip or all clips?
questions.say_example: <Track or clip> is set to <actual level>. You requested <requested level>.

questions.question: Are the audio tracks required by the edit included in the mix?
questions.why: The export could lose the voiceover or include unwanted sound.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The export could lose the voiceover or include unwanted sound.
questions.check: What are the mute, solo, and enabled state of each audio track before export?
questions.say_example: <Required track> is excluded from the mix.

questions.question: Does the audio effect apply only to the intended clip or track?
questions.why: Other voices or sounds could be changed unintentionally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Other voices or sounds could be changed unintentionally.
questions.check: What is the applied audio effect, and is its scope set to the single clip or the whole track?
questions.say_example: <Effect> applies to <actual scope>. You asked to change <requested scope>.

questions.question: Did audio processing preserve the words and natural sound that should remain?
questions.why: Cleaning up the sound could also damage the recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Cleaning up the sound could also damage the recording.
questions.check: When listening to the processed passage against the unprocessed original, is there any change to the words or background sound?
questions.say_example: The processed passage has <observed sound problem> at <time>.

children.label: Align sound with picture
children.note: 6.4.1 positions the sound, 6.4.2 trims its boundaries, 6.4.3 extends music where needed, and 6.4.4 sets fades; check the result with 7.4 and repeat after picture edits

questions.question: Does the editor report a new offset between media that should stay synchronized?
questions.why: The edit may need a synchronization review before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The edit may need a synchronization review before continuing.
questions.check: What are the signed offset and affected linked media identifiers? Color alone does not prove an offset.
questions.say_example: The editor reports <offset> between <paired media>. It should stay at <target>.

questions.question: Does the sound occur with the intended visible event?
questions.why: The action and its sound could appear disconnected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The action and its sound could appear disconnected.
questions.check: What is the timestamp of the sound cue, against the timestamp of the visible event it should match?
questions.say_example: <Sound> occurs <observed timing> relative to <event>.

questions.question: Does the audio end with the intended closing passage?
questions.why: The finished video may end abruptly or keep playing after its intended end.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The finished video may end abruptly or keep playing after its intended end.
questions.check: What does the last moment of the audio track sound like, against the last moment of the video?
questions.say_example: The ending cuts off <word or sound> at <time>.

questions.question: Does the selected audio begin with the intended passage?
questions.why: The sound may start abruptly or miss its intended opening.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The sound may start abruptly or miss its intended opening.
questions.check: What does the first moment of the selected audio sound like, against the passage it was meant to start with?
questions.say_example: The audio starts with <actual passage>. You asked it to start with <requested passage>.

questions.question: Does the repeated music cover the intended passage without an audible break?
questions.why: The music could sound interrupted or unfinished.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The music could sound interrupted or unfinished.
questions.check: When listening across the join where the music repeats, is there any audible break or repeat?
questions.say_example: There is <audible problem> at the music join at <time>.

questions.question: Do the fades still let you hear the words and sounds that matter?
questions.why: Part of the speech may disappear even though the clip remains on the timeline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Part of the speech may disappear even though the clip remains on the timeline.
questions.check: When listening through the fade, does any word or sound become inaudible during it?
questions.say_example: The fade hides <word or sound> at <time>.

children.label: Review the edited sequence
children.note: 7.1 plays the relevant passage; use 7.2 through 7.5 to check cuts, visible content, sound, and total length; return to the operation that caused a problem; use 7.6 only when preview performance prevents judging the edit

questions.question: Does the cut preserve the intended continuity of the passage?
questions.why: The viewer may struggle to follow the action or sentence.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer may struggle to follow the action or sentence.
questions.check: Do the frames immediately before and after the cut show any visible jump, mismatch, or repeated action?
questions.say_example: The cut at <time> <observed continuity problem>.

questions.question: Are there unintended flash frames or black gaps in the rendered sequence?
questions.why: The video could briefly flash an unrelated image or black frame.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video could briefly flash an unrelated image or black frame.
questions.check: Do the frames at each cut point show a frame that does not belong to either adjacent clip, or a black frame?
questions.say_example: There is <unexpected frame or gap> at <time>.

questions.question: Does the music or added sound cover any required speech?
questions.why: The viewer could miss the explanation even when the voice track sounds clear on its own.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The viewer could miss the explanation even when the voice track sounds clear on its own.
questions.check: When listening to the passage with music or effects playing under speech, does any word become inaudible?
questions.say_example: <Music or effect> covers the words <passage> at <time range>.

questions.question: Does the complete sound mix preserve the requested balance?
questions.why: An added effect or music bed could overwhelm the intended scene sound.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An added effect or music bed could overwhelm the intended scene sound.
questions.check: When listening to the mix, what is the relative loudness of the named sound against what was requested?
questions.say_example: <Sound> is <observed prominence> at <time>. You asked for <requested prominence>.

questions.question: Does the edited sequence meet the requested duration?
questions.why: The edit may be too long or too short for its intended use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The edit may be too long or too short for its intended use.
questions.check: What are the total active sequence duration and its time units?
questions.say_example: The sequence lasts <actual duration>. Your limit is <requested limit>.

children.label: Export and check video
children.note: 8.1 chooses the output kind; 8.2 sets the range; 8.3 through 8.6 configure quality, captions, and the file destination; 8.7 reviews requirements before 8.8 starts the job; 8.9 checks whether the export has finished; 8.10 opens the saved output; 8.11 is optional and requires explicit authorization to publish or link an external account

questions.question: Will this export produce the kind of deliverable you requested?
questions.why: The resulting files may not be usable for the requested purpose.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The resulting files may not be usable for the requested purpose.
questions.check: What are the selected export type and mode, including single-file versus individual-clips output?
questions.say_example: This export will produce <actual type>. You asked for <requested type>.

questions.question: Does the export include the requested sequence range?
questions.why: The export could omit the opening or ending, or include unwanted material.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The export could omit the opening or ending, or include unwanted material.
questions.check: What are the export range mode, start, end, and duration for the active sequence?
questions.say_example: The export is set from <start> to <end>. The requested range is <requested range>.

questions.question: Does the export resolution match what you need to deliver?
questions.why: The delivered video could have the wrong size or lose required detail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video could have the wrong size or lose required detail.
questions.check: What are the selected export width and height, separately from the preview resolution?
questions.say_example: The export is set to <actual dimensions>. You requested <required dimensions>.

questions.question: Does the export still use the frame rate you set?
questions.why: The delivered video could have a different frame rate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video could have a different frame rate.
questions.check: What is the selected export frame rate after the control settles? File-size estimates do not establish the selected rate.
questions.say_example: The export frame rate is <actual>. You requested <requested>.

questions.question: Does the export match what you need to deliver?
questions.why: The file could be rejected or displayed incorrectly by its intended destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The file could be rejected or displayed incorrectly by its intended destination.
questions.check: What are the selected export format and the encoding properties specified by the request?
questions.say_example: <Export property> is set to <actual>. The delivery requirement is <requested>.

questions.question: Will captions be delivered in the form you requested?
questions.why: People who need captions may not receive them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: People who need captions may not receive them.
questions.check: What are the selected subtitle export mode and any selected caption track?
questions.say_example: Captions are set to <actual mode>. You requested <required mode>.

questions.question: Does the export use the requested filename?
questions.why: The delivered file may be hard to identify or be mistaken for another version.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered file may be hard to identify or be mistaken for another version.
questions.check: What are the output filename and extension in the save or render dialog?
questions.say_example: The output is named <actual filename>. You requested <requested filename>.

questions.question: Is the file being saved to the destination you requested?
questions.why: The file could be hard to find or placed in the wrong account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The file could be hard to find or placed in the wrong account.
questions.check: What are the selected save destination and account, if one is displayed?
questions.say_example: The selected destination is <actual>. You requested <requested destination>.

questions.question: Do you want to replace the existing file?
questions.why: An earlier finished version could be lost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An earlier finished version could be lost.
questions.verify_form: Is replacing this existing output file authorized?
questions.check: What are the existing filename, destination, and replacement warning?
questions.say_example: <Filename> already exists in <destination>. Replace it?

questions.question: Does the estimated export size exceed a stated delivery limit?
questions.why: The file may be too large to upload or deliver.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The file may be too large to upload or deliver.
questions.check: What are the estimated output file size and its units?
questions.say_example: The estimated file size is <estimate>. The delivery limit is <limit>.

questions.question: Does the destination have enough space for the export?
questions.why: The export may fail before the file is saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The export may fail before the file is saved.
questions.check: What are the free space for the selected destination and the displayed space requirement or exact insufficient-space warning?
questions.say_example: <Destination> has <available space>. The export requires <required space>.

questions.question: Does the export add a watermark you didn't ask for?
questions.why: The delivered picture could contain unwanted branding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered picture could contain unwanted branding.
questions.check: What are the exact watermark warning and the feature or asset it applies to?
questions.say_example: The export warning says <watermark> will be added because of <selected item>.

questions.question: Did the editor report that this export failed?
questions.why: The expected output may not exist or may be incomplete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The expected output may not exist or may be incomplete.
questions.check: What captured error or failure message is there, and does it belong to the current export job?
questions.say_example: The export failed with <error>. <Output> has not been confirmed.

questions.question: Does the editor confirm that each requested export finished?
questions.why: The task could be reported complete while a file is still missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The task could be reported complete while a file is still missing.
questions.check: Is there a completion or save confirmation naming the output, or a saved-file listing that identifies it? Progress, Render All, and a thumbnail alone are insufficient.
questions.say_example: The editor reports that <output> was saved to <destination>.

questions.question: Did the automated sound check report a restriction or warning?
questions.why: The service may limit how the video can be delivered or heard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The service may limit how the video can be delivered or heard.
questions.check: What are the exact result and any stated restriction?
questions.say_example: The sound check reports <warning>. It says <stated effect on delivery>.

questions.question: Does the saved video open and play through the requested content?
questions.why: A successful export message could still accompany an unusable file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A successful export message could still accompany an unusable file.
questions.check: When opening and playing the saved file, is there any point where it stops, skips, or fails to match the requested content?
questions.say_example: The saved file <filename> has <observed playback problem> at <time>.

questions.question: Does the saved file match what you need to deliver?
questions.why: The exported file could be rejected even though the settings appeared correct.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The exported file could be rejected even though the settings appeared correct.
questions.check: What are the saved file's properties (resolution, duration, format), against the stated delivery requirements?
questions.say_example: <Filename> has <actual property>. The delivery requires <requested property>.

questions.question: Are the requested captions present and usable in the delivered files?
questions.why: The delivered video may be inaccessible to people relying on captions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video may be inaccessible to people relying on captions.
questions.check: When opening the delivered file, is the requested caption track present and does it display text?
questions.say_example: The delivered <file or track> has <observed caption problem>.

questions.question: Does the delivered file contain the latest changes you approved?
questions.why: The recipient could receive an outdated edit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The recipient could receive an outdated edit.
questions.check: What are the saved file's modification time or content, against the version that was approved?
questions.say_example: <Filename> still contains <earlier content>. The approved version has <changed content>.

questions.question: Did the export introduce a visible problem the approved version doesn't have?
questions.why: The delivered video could differ from the edit that was approved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delivered video could differ from the edit that was approved.
questions.check: Is there any visible difference between the exported file at the relevant time and the approved sequence?
questions.say_example: The exported file has <visible problem> at <time>. The approved sequence does not.

questions.question: Do you want to publish this video to this account and audience?
questions.why: The video could be sent to an unintended account or audience.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The video could be sent to an unintended account or audience.
questions.verify_form: Is publishing or uploading this video authorized for this account and audience?
questions.check: What are the pending output, destination account, and audience or visibility setting? Do not assume an upload is public.
questions.say_example: <Video> will be uploaded to <account> with <visibility>. Upload it?

questions.question: Is this publishing connection asking for more access than you agreed to?
questions.why: The editor could gain more access to the account than intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The editor could gain more access to the account than intended.
questions.verify_form: Does the publishing connection grant only the access you approved?
questions.check: What are the actual authorization prompt, account identity, and permissions requested?
questions.say_example: <App> is asking for <permissions> on <account>. Allow that access?

questions.question: Does the destination confirm that the authorized upload finished?
questions.why: The local export may exist while the delivered copy is missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The local export may exist while the delivered copy is missing.
questions.check: What does the destination’s completed-upload confirmation, or file listing identifying this output, show?
questions.say_example: The destination confirms <output> finished uploading to <account>.

children.label: Manage the saved files
children.note: 9.1 preserves editing progress throughout the edit; the remaining operations are optional file management after a separate request; 9.2 inspects the saved project; 9.3 verifies its source media; 9.4 and 9.5 require an explicit decision about what to delete and what to retain

questions.question: Have the latest project changes been saved before leaving the editor?
questions.why: The latest edits may be lost when the project closes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The latest edits may be lost when the project closes.
questions.check: What are the current save status or explicit unsaved-changes warning? An Edited label during ongoing work is normal.
questions.say_example: The editor still reports unsaved changes in <project>.

questions.question: Is the editable project saved where you asked to keep it?
questions.why: The editable project could be unavailable or stored in an unintended account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The editable project could be unavailable or stored in an unintended account.
questions.check: What are the saved project location and account or cloud status?
questions.say_example: Saved the project in <the local Videos folder> - you asked for <the cloud drive>

questions.question: Are the source files that should be retained still available after cleanup?
questions.why: The project may no longer be editable from its original media.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The project may no longer be editable from its original media.
questions.check: What does the file listing at the retained location show for each source file that was marked to keep?
questions.say_example: <Required source> is no longer available after cleanup.

questions.question: Does the saved project reopen with the latest edit and required media?
questions.why: Further editing could require rebuilding work or locating missing sources.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Further editing could require rebuilding work or locating missing sources.
questions.check: When reopening the saved project, does it show the latest edit and locate its required media without a missing-file warning?
questions.say_example: The saved project has <observed reopening problem>.

questions.question: Is deleting this project part of the cleanup you asked for?
questions.why: The editable sequence could be lost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The editable sequence could be lost.
questions.verify_form: Is deleting this project covered by your cleanup request?
questions.check: What are the project identity and the exact deletion dialog, including any affected media?
questions.say_example: This will delete <project>. The dialog says <what happens to its media>. Delete it?

questions.question: Is removing these source files part of the cleanup you asked for?
questions.why: Other projects or future revisions could lose their original media.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Other projects or future revisions could lose their original media.
questions.verify_form: Is removing these source files covered by your cleanup request?
questions.check: What are the selected file identities and the deletion warning, including any trash or permanent-delete distinction?
questions.say_example: This will remove <source files>. They may still be needed by other edits. Remove them?
